title: U.S. House · Texas's 28th Congressional District
area: South Texas along the border, from Laredo (Webb County) north toward San Antonio.

context.text: Texas redrew its congressional district boundaries in August 2025 ahead of the 2026 elections. Ballotpedia identifies this race as a battleground: during redistricting, the district was redrawn to one Donald Trump would have carried 54.8%-44.4% in 2024, compared to 53.1%-45.8% under the prior lines, making it one of 23 Democratic-held U.S. House seats up in 2026 that Trump won in 2024.

Henry Cuellar was indicted in May 2024 on federal charges of bribery, unlawful foreign influence, and money laundering, alleging that he and his wife accepted $600,000 from an Azerbaijan-linked oil-and-gas company and a Mexican bank; House Democratic rules required him to leave his Appropriations subcommittee post after the indictment. President Trump pardoned Cuellar and his wife in December 2025, and Cuellar retook the subcommittee leadership position; the Cook Political Report subsequently moved its rating of the race from Toss-up to Lean Democratic.

In the March 3, 2026 primaries, Cuellar defeated Ricardo Villarreal and Andrew Vantine 58.1% to 37.0% to 5.0% for the Democratic nomination, and Tano Tijerina defeated Eileen Day 74.3% to 25.7% for the Republican nomination. Marlon Duran advanced as the Green Party's nominee from its March 21, 2026 convention.

summary.text: Henry Cuellar is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for Texas's 28th District, in office since 2005. A Laredo native, he is a lawyer and educator who served in the Texas House and as Texas Secretary of State before Congress, and he serves on the House Appropriations Committee. He was indicted on federal bribery charges in 2024 and pardoned by President Trump in December 2025; he has said he is innocent of the allegations.

background.text: Born in Laredo, Texas, in 1955; according to his congressional biography, he was the eldest of eight children of migrant farmworkers and the first in his family to attend college.

Earned an associate degree from Laredo Community College (1976), a bachelor's degree in foreign service from Georgetown University (1978), a J.D. from the University of Texas at Austin (1981), a master's in international trade from Texas A&M International University (1982), and a Ph.D. in government from UT Austin (1998).

His congressional biography also lists a professional certificate in homeland security from Texas A&M's Bush School of Government and a Master of Arts in Defense and Strategic Studies from the U.S. Naval War College, completed in spring 2025.
Before elective office he worked as a lawyer in private practice; his congressional biography also lists U.S. customs brokerage and teaching at Texas A&M International University and Laredo College.
Served in the Texas House of Representatives from 1987 to 2001 and as Texas Secretary of State in 2001.
First sworn into the U.S. House in 2005 and re-elected since, most recently in 2024 by the narrowest margin of his career.

Serves on the House Appropriations Committee and, according to his official biography, is Ranking Member of its Subcommittee on Homeland Security and a member of the Defense and Military Construction, Veterans Affairs subcommittees.

Indicted by the Justice Department on May 3, 2024, on counts including bribery, unlawful foreign influence, and money laundering; he and his wife pleaded not guilty and he said both are innocent. President Trump pardoned both of them on December 3, 2025.
According to his congressional biography, he lives in Laredo with his wife, Imelda, and they have two daughters; he holds a third-degree black belt in Shotokan karate.

record.text: Was indicted in May 2024 on federal charges of bribery, unlawful foreign influence, and money laundering; House Democratic rules required him to leave his House Appropriations Homeland Security subcommittee leadership post after the indictment.
Was pardoned by President Trump in December 2025 and retook his leadership position on the Appropriations Homeland Security subcommittee.

Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations in the 119th Congress (2025-2026), including as Ranking Member of its Homeland Security subcommittee and as a member of its Military Construction-Veterans Affairs and Defense subcommittees.

candidates.name: Tano Tijerina
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 74.3% of the vote

summary.text: Tano Tijerina is the Webb County Judge, a post he has held since 2015, and the Republican nominee in Texas's 28th District. A former minor league baseball player and rancher, he was elected county judge as a Democrat and switched to the Republican Party in December 2024. He won the March 2026 Republican primary and is running on border security, affordability and public safety.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in fitness and sports from Texas A&M International University.
Played minor league baseball and worked in the ranching industry before his judgeship; Ballotpedia also lists him as executive vice president of the Precept Ministries Spanish Board.

Elected Webb County Judge in 2014 as a Democrat and took office in 2015; he won re-election in 2018 (76.3% against Republican Alfonso Casso) and in 2022 (no general election was held after he advanced from the Democratic primary unopposed).
Switched to the Republican Party in December 2024, saying, according to the Texas Tribune, that the Democratic Party no longer aligned with his values.
Announced his campaign for Congress on December 2, 2025; his third term as county judge runs through December 31, 2026.
Won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 74.3% of the vote over Eileen Day.
Says his record as county judge includes cutting property taxes five times, delivering $20 million in utility relief, and expanding healthcare access in Webb County.

priorities.text: His campaign website lists border security and immigration enforcement, lowering taxes and cutting federal regulation, and supporting cryptocurrency innovation among his priorities.

positions.summary: Says the border must be secured, the law enforced, and illegal crossings stopped, while backing a practical, bipartisan path for immigrants who came 'the right way.'
Says he would fight to lower taxes for working families and small businesses and cut federal regulations, citing his record lowering property taxes five times in ten years as Webb County Judge.

record.text: As Webb County Judge, lowered property taxes five times over ten years, according to his campaign.

candidates.name: Marlon Duran
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced as the Green Party's nominee from its March 21, 2026 state convention

summary.text: Marlón Durán is the Green Party nominee in Texas's 28th District. The San Antonio Report describes him as a progressive activist who has worked on local and federal campaigns.

background.text: According to the San Antonio Report, Durán is a progressive activist who has worked on local and federal campaigns.
Has a degree in organizational leadership from South Texas College and works as a professional translator, according to the San Antonio Report.
